O.outcome_detail: DIF in preclinical course assessment items

result.effect: Anatomy: 7/49 items (14%); Histology: 2/40 items (5%); Physiology: 3/45 items (7%)

cells.quote: For sex, the χ2 statistic was significant for seven items indicating that 14% of the anatomy test items showed statistically significant DIF, favoring male students.
cells.note: The study reports item-level differential functioning favoring male students; it does not provide a standardized effect size.

O.outcome_detail: DIF in preclinical course assessment items

result.effect: Anatomy: 5/49 items (approximately 10%); Histology: 5/40 items (approximately 13%); Physiology: 2/45 items (4%)

cells.quote: For race, five items (approximately 10%) had statistically significant DIF, favoring white students.
cells.note: The study operationalized race as White versus non-White because some racial groups were too small for robust IRT analysis; it does not provide a standardized effect size.

D.treatment: students in histology and physiology assessments

result.effect: Histology CFI 0.99, RMSEA 0.007; Physiology CFI 0.96, RMSEA 0.011; Anatomy CFI 0.88, RMSEA 0.041

cells.quote: Based on Table 2, Histology and Physiology had excellent model-data fit, since the M2 statistic was not significant, the CFI and TLI indices were above 0.90, and the RMSEA and SRMSR were below 0.08. For anatomy, despite the CFI and TLI indices were relatively lower than the recommended threshold, the RMSEA and SRMSR were very good indicating model-data fit.
cells.note: This cell codes the reported comparison of model-data fit across the three course assessments; the text does not report an instructional treatment.
